newsitem.title: UK: Briton sues over televised suicide bid.
newsitem.headline: Briton sues over televised suicide bid.

text.p: A man whose suicide attempt was caught on closed circuit television and then broadcast on national television won the right on Friday to seek compensation in Britain's High Court.
Geoffery Peck, 42, was filmed by cameras as he tried to cut his wrists with a kitchen knife in a street in Brentwood, east of London, last year.
The local council handed the film to BBC television, which used it in a crime programme. Stills from the footage also appeared in a local newspaper.
The council argued that distributing the film helped to highlight the value of closed circuit television (CCTV) in deterring crime.
But Peck sought compensation from the council, saying his privacy was invaded by the "cheap and salacious" use of the footage.
He was in a depressed state when he tried to kill himself after learning that his girlfriend was terminally ill.
"The consequences of the release of the CCTV film to the media have been extremely distressing and humiliating for Mr Peck," said his lawyer Richard Gordon.
A judge ruled that Peck could sue the council in the High Court for invasion of privacy.
